canh-suon-nau-sau.name: Northern Vietnamese pork rib and dracontomelon soup
aliases: Northern pork rib soup with dracontomelon
Pork ribs and dracontomelon sour soup
canh-suon-nau-sau.serving_basis: One pot of gently sour soup for four people to share with a family meal.
canh-suon-nau-sau.description: This familiar Northern Vietnamese summer soup pairs tender pork ribs and tomatoes with the clean sourness of green dracontomelon. The fruit is simmered separately and mashed so its acidity can be added gradually; scallion and Vietnamese coriander finish the broth.
canh-suon-nau-sau.finished_dish: A lightly golden-red clear broth with tender ribs, tomato wedges and a gentle sour finish.
canh-suon-nau-sau.serving: Serve hot with steamed rice and a savory main dish. Add the dracontomelon liquid gradually so the soup stays pleasantly sour rather than sharp.
tips: Blanch and rinse the ribs for a clearer broth.
Simmer and mash the dracontomelon separately, then strain and add its liquid a little at a time.
Add scallions and Vietnamese coriander at the end to keep their aroma.
search_terms: Northern pork rib soup with dracontomelon
canh-suon-nau-sau.image_alt: Northern Vietnamese pork rib and dracontomelon soup with tomato, scallion and Vietnamese coriander; Bếp Việt image on a transparent background.

ingredients.name: Pork ribs
ingredients.notes: Cut into serving pieces; choose ribs with some meat.

ingredients.name: Green dracontomelon
ingredients.notes: Scrape and score lightly; adjust the number to the fruit's acidity.

ingredients.name: Tomatoes
ingredients.notes: Divide between the sautéed base and the final simmer.

ingredients.name: Shallots
ingredients.notes: Peel and slice.

ingredients.name: Fish sauce
ingredients.notes: Start with a modest amount and season again after adding the sour liquid.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.notes: Use a little for blanching and the rest to season.

ingredients.name: Chicken seasoning powder
ingredients.notes: Optional if the broth already tastes full.

ingredients.name: Scallions
ingredients.notes: Wash and finely slice.

ingredients.name: Vietnamese coriander
ingredients.notes: Wash and finely slice.

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.notes: Use hot water for simmering the ribs.

preparation_steps: Cut the ribs into serving pieces, blanch briefly in salted boiling water, discard the water, rinse the ribs and drain.
Season the ribs with some fish sauce, salt and seasoning powder for about 15 minutes. Prepare the dracontomelon, tomatoes, shallots, scallions and Vietnamese coriander.
cooking_steps: Sauté the shallots until fragrant. Add half the tomatoes and cook until soft; add the ribs and sear lightly.
Pour in hot water, bring to a boil, skim the foam and simmer gently for 30–35 minutes until the ribs are tender.
Simmer the dracontomelon separately with a little water for about 5 minutes. Mash and strain it. Add the remaining tomatoes to the rib pot and cook for 3–4 minutes.
Season the soup, then add the sour dracontomelon liquid gradually to taste. Turn off the heat and add scallions and Vietnamese coriander.
canh-suon-nau-sau.time_note: About 60 minutes when cooked sequentially; parallel prep can shorten the total time.

ca-ro-phi-kho-tuong-khe.name: Northern Vietnamese tilapia braised with fermented soybean paste and starfruit
aliases: Tilapia braised with fermented soybean and starfruit
Rice-field perch braised with B?n soybean and starfruit
ca-ro-phi-kho-tuong-khe.serving_basis: Three or four small tilapia braised with starfruit for four servings.
ca-ro-phi-kho-tuong-khe.description: This Northern-style braise combines the savory depth of Bần fermented soybean paste with the mild tartness of green starfruit. The fish is layered with starfruit and simmered gently until firm and coated in a lightly thickened sauce; turmeric leaf adds a regional aroma when available.
ca-ro-phi-kho-tuong-khe.finished_dish: Intact pieces of fish coated in a golden-brown soybean sauce, with softened but pleasantly tart starfruit.
ca-ro-phi-kho-tuong-khe.serving: Serve hot in the clay pot with steamed rice and boiled greens. Taste before adding extra salt because fermented soybean paste varies in saltiness.
tips: Drain the fish well and avoid turning it while braising so it stays intact.
Bần soybean paste varies in saltiness; dilute a little and season gradually.
Keep the simmer gentle and spoon the sauce over the fish instead of stirring.
search_terms: tilapia braised with fermented soybean paste and starfruit
ca-ro-phi-kho-tuong-khe.image_alt: Clay pot of Northern Vietnamese tilapia braised with Bần soybean paste, green starfruit and turmeric leaves; Bếp Việt image on a transparent background.
suggested_pairings: Minced pork and malabar spinach soup

ingredients.name: Small tilapia
ingredients.notes: Clean and remove gills and innards; small climbing perch can be used at the same total weight.

ingredients.name: Sour green starfruit
ingredients.notes: Wash, trim the ridges and slice thickly.

ingredients.name: Bần fermented soybean paste
ingredients.notes: Stir well and start with less if the paste is salty.

ingredients.name: Pork belly
ingredients.notes: Slice thinly to add a little richness.

ingredients.name: Shallots
ingredients.notes: Peel and mince.

ingredients.name: Cane molasses
ingredients.notes: Use a small amount to round out the savory soybean flavor.

ingredients.name: Turmeric powder
ingredients.notes: Use lightly for color; fresh turmeric may be substituted.

ingredients.name: Fresh turmeric leaves
ingredients.notes: Wash and thinly slice; omit if unavailable.

ingredients.name: Red chili
ingredients.notes: Leave whole or remove seeds to control heat.

ingredients.name: Ground black pepper
ingredients.notes: Divide between the marinade and serving.

ingredients.name: Neutral cooking oil
ingredients.notes: For sautéing shallots and rendering the pork belly slightly.

ingredients.name: Hot water
ingredients.notes: Add gradually; the fish does not need to be submerged.

preparation_steps: Rinse and drain the fish, then score both sides lightly. Marinate with some soybean paste, molasses, pepper, turmeric and shallots for 20 minutes.
Trim and slice the starfruit; wash and thinly slice the turmeric leaves. Slice the pork belly and prepare a clay or heavy-bottomed pot.
cooking_steps: Heat the pot, sauté half the shallots in oil, and cook the pork belly until just firm.
Layer starfruit on the bottom, arrange the fish on top and tuck the remaining starfruit around it. Pour in the marinade.
Bring to a gentle boil for about 2 minutes. Add hot water to about halfway up the fish. Cover loosely and braise on low for 30–35 minutes; tilt the pot occasionally instead of turning the fish.
Add the remaining soybean paste a little at a time, taste, and braise for 8–10 minutes until the sauce lightly thickens. Finish with turmeric leaf, chili and pepper.
keywords: tilapia braised with fermented soybean and starfruit
ca-ro-phi-kho-tuong-khe.time_note: About 90 minutes when cooked sequentially; parallel prep can shorten the total time.

ga-hap-la-truc.name: An Giang chicken steamed with lá trúc leaves
aliases: An Giang chicken steamed with citrus leaves
Seven Mountains chicken steamed with citrus leaves
ga-hap-la-truc.serving_basis: One 1.2 kg free-range chicken, divided into four servings.
ga-hap-la-truc.description: Chicken steamed with lá trúc is a rustic dish associated with the Bảy Núi area of An Giang. The leaves and fruit have a stronger, more aromatic citrus character than ordinary lime; steaming the seasoned chicken over the leaves keeps the meat moist and fragrant.
ga-hap-la-truc.finished_dish: Tender, juicy chicken with pale golden skin and a clear citrus-leaf aroma, served with chili, salt and trúc juice.
ga-hap-la-truc.serving: Chop the chicken just before serving and eat hot with fresh vegetables or shredded banana blossom. Serve the chili salt separately for dipping.
tips: Use young or medium-aged leaves; remove tough ribs from older leaves to avoid bitterness.
Steam until the thickest part of the thigh reaches 74°C.
If stuffing the cavity with glass noodles and mushrooms, do not pack it tightly.
search_terms: An Giang chicken steamed with lá trúc
ga-hap-la-truc.image_alt: An Giang chicken steamed with lá trúc leaves, served with shredded banana blossom and citrus chili salt; Bếp Việt image on a transparent background.
suggested_pairings: Sầu đâu salad with dried snakehead

ingredients.name: Free-range chicken
ingredients.notes: Clean and steam whole; a 1–1.2 kg bird cooks evenly in most home steamers.

ingredients.name: Lá trúc leaves
ingredients.notes: Wash and drain; reserve a few leaves to slice for serving.

ingredients.name: Trúc fruit
ingredients.notes: Use one for seasoning the chicken and one for the dipping salt.

ingredients.name: Ginger
ingredients.notes: Bruise half for cleaning and slice the rest.

ingredients.name: Garlic
ingredients.notes: Peel and mince.

ingredients.name: Fish sauce
ingredients.notes: Season lightly because the chicken is also served with dipping salt.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.notes: Divide between the marinade and dipping salt.

ingredients.name: Ground black pepper
ingredients.notes: For the marinade.

ingredients.name: Fresh chili
ingredients.notes: Mince some for the dipping salt; optional.

ingredients.name: Shredded banana blossom
ingredients.notes: Rinse briefly in lemon water and drain for serving.

preparation_steps: Rub the chicken with salt and bruised ginger, rinse and pat dry. Marinate with minced garlic, pepper, fish sauce, a little salt and juice from one trúc fruit for about 20 minutes.
Wash the leaves and remove tough ribs if needed. Line the steamer or a heatproof bowl with most of the leaves; prepare the reserved leaves, remaining fruit and dipping salt.
cooking_steps: Place the chicken on the leaves, add a few slices of ginger and cover tightly. Steam for 35–40 minutes depending on size; check that the thickest part of the thigh reaches 74°C or the juices run clear.
Rest the chicken for 5 minutes, then chop into portions and top with sliced leaves.
Mix salt, pepper, chili and trúc juice for dipping. Serve with shredded banana blossom.
ga-hap-la-truc.time_note: About 85 minutes when cooked sequentially; parallel prep can shorten the total time.

muop-xao-trung.name: Vietnamese stir-fried luffa with egg
muop-xao-trung.serving_basis: One shared vegetable side dish for four people.
muop-xao-trung.description: Stir-fried luffa with egg is a quick home-style side dish: tender, juicy luffa and soft golden egg come together with scallion. Cooking the luffa only until just tender preserves its green color and natural sweetness.
muop-xao-trung.finished_dish: Bright green luffa slices that are tender but not mushy, coated with softly set egg and finished with scallion and pepper.
muop-xao-trung.serving: Serve hot with steamed rice and a more savory main. This dish is best just after cooking because the luffa releases liquid as it stands.
tips: Choose young, firm luffa and cut it thick enough to hold its shape.
Keep the pan hot and add the egg when the luffa is nearly tender.
Stop stirring as soon as the egg has set to keep the luffa from becoming watery.
muop-xao-trung.image_alt: Vietnamese green luffa stir-fried with soft golden egg, scallion and pepper; Bếp Việt image on a transparent background.

ingredients.name: Angled luffa or fragrant luffa
ingredients.notes: Peel lightly, halve lengthwise and cut into 1.5–2 cm diagonal slices.

ingredients.name: Duck eggs
ingredients.notes: Lightly beat with a pinch of salt.

ingredients.name: Shallots
ingredients.notes: Peel and slice.

ingredients.name: Scallions
ingredients.notes: Wash and finely slice.

ingredients.name: Fish sauce
ingredients.notes: Season once the luffa begins to soften.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.notes: Use a small pinch for the eggs.

ingredients.name: Ground black pepper
ingredients.notes: Finish the dish with pepper.

ingredients.name: Neutral cooking oil
ingredients.notes: For sautéing the shallots and luffa.

preparation_steps: Wash, peel lightly and cut the luffa into 1.5–2 cm diagonal slices. Slice the shallots and scallions.
Beat the eggs lightly with a pinch of salt. Have the seasonings ready because the stir-fry cooks quickly.
cooking_steps: Heat the oil in a pan and sauté the shallots until fragrant. Add the luffa and stir-fry over medium heat for 2–3 minutes.
Season with fish sauce and cook until the luffa is just translucent and tender but still holds its shape. Add one or two tablespoons of water if the pan is dry.
Pour the egg around the pan. Wait 10–15 seconds, then fold gently until the egg is just set and coats the luffa. Add scallions and pepper, then turn off the heat.
muop-xao-trung.time_note: About 20 minutes when cooked sequentially; parallel prep can shorten the total time.

canh-khoai-so-lac-dau-phu-chay.name: Vegetarian taro soup with peanuts and tofu
aliases: Vegetarian taro soup with peanuts and tofu
Taro soup with peanuts and tofu
canh-khoai-so-lac-dau-phu-chay.serving_basis: One pot of mild vegetarian soup for four people to share.
canh-khoai-so-lac-dau-phu-chay.description: This simple vegetarian soup combines the earthy sweetness of taro and peanuts with golden fried tofu and fragrant Vietnamese coriander. Simmer the peanuts until tender before adding the taro so the ingredients finish cooking together without the taro breaking apart.
canh-khoai-so-lac-dau-phu-chay.finished_dish: A mild broth with tender taro, nutty peanuts and tofu pieces that hold their shape, finished with fresh Vietnamese coriander.
canh-khoai-so-lac-dau-phu-chay.serving: Ladle into a large bowl and serve hot with steamed rice and a vegetable or braised vegetarian dish. If starting with dried peanuts, soak and boil them separately first.
tips: Use fully cooked peanuts to shorten the cooking time; if cooking from dried, add them before the taro.
Wear gloves when peeling taro if its skin irritates your hands; rinse and drain it promptly.
Add fried tofu near the end and simmer gently so it does not break.
search_terms: Vietnamese vegetarian taro peanut tofu soup
canh khoai sọ nấu lạc đậu phụ
canh-khoai-so-lac-dau-phu-chay.image_alt: Vietnamese vegetarian taro soup with peanuts, golden tofu and Vietnamese coriander; Bếp Việt image on a transparent background.
suggested_pairings: Water spinach stir-fried with fermented bean curd

ingredients.name: Taro
ingredients.notes: Peel, wash and cut into bite-size pieces.

ingredients.name: Cooked peanuts
ingredients.notes: Peel the hard outer skin; the thin reddish skin may remain.

ingredients.name: Firm tofu
ingredients.notes: Cut into cubes and pat dry before frying.

ingredients.name: Vietnamese coriander
ingredients.notes: Wash and finely slice.

ingredients.name: Neutral cooking oil
ingredients.notes: For frying the tofu.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.notes: Season gradually to taste.

ingredients.name: Sugar
ingredients.notes: Optional; use a small amount to round out the broth.

ingredients.name: Water or vegetable stock
ingredients.notes: Use plain water or a mild vegetable broth.

preparation_steps: Rinse the cooked peanuts and drain. Peel and wash the taro, then cut into bite-size pieces.
Cut the tofu into cubes and pat dry. Wash and slice the Vietnamese coriander.
cooking_steps: Heat the oil and fry the tofu until lightly golden on both sides; drain.
Bring the peanuts and water to a boil, then simmer gently for about 10 minutes so the peanuts are hot and tender.
Add the taro and simmer gently for 15–20 minutes until tender but not falling apart. Skim the broth if needed.
Season with salt and a little sugar if desired. Add the tofu and simmer for 3 minutes. Finish with Vietnamese coriander and turn off the heat.
canh-khoai-so-lac-dau-phu-chay.time_note: About 60 minutes when cooked sequentially; parallel prep can shorten the total time.
